svg.text: A fifth of this register is flagged on land. Removing it would delete the shore.
anyone about to exclude flagged records before analysing OBIS
whether a quality flag marks an error or a habitat
dropping the flagged rows moves any finding in this recipe
the two big flags select opposite animals
share of each class's records carrying each flag
over 4% below the sea floor — rugged bottom
Nothing sits in the top right. A class is either counted from the shore or
found on broken ground, and almost never both. Seabirds are half on land
because that is where people stand to count them; sea urchins are a tenth
below the sea floor because the bathymetry raster is coarser than the rock
they live on. Neither is a mistake in the record.
figure 8's crossing depth, re-measured with the flagged records excluded
share of the class's records removed by cleaning
change in the crossing depth, metres
never reaches a tenth, before or after
Every mark sits on the zero line. Cleaning removes up to 23% of a class's
records and moves not one of the seven crossings — seagrasses 20 m, kelp 30
m, red algae 50 m, green algae 70 m, and the three controls still never
reach a tenth. The share of all records in the top 200 m goes from 88.0% to
87.6%. The flags fall roughly where each group already is, so a within-bin
ratio divides them out — the same reason figure 8 worked.
OBIS v3 statistics/qc and occurrence with flags/exclude, fetched 2026-09-19 against 229,671,953 records. statistics/qc and a filtered count disagree
on ON_LAND — 43,236,520 against 34,582,170 — because the qc table counts everything ever ingested including rows dropped before indexing, while the
filter counts what a query returns; the filter count is used, being the population every other figure drew from. Both parameters were verified:
flags=BANANA returns 0 rather than the total, and banana=ON_LAND returns the unfiltered total, which is what four other parameters in this API do
silently. Cleaning here means excluding ON_LAND, DEPTH_EXCEEDS_BATH, NO_MATCH, NOT_MARINE.
